newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up on bargain hunting.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended higher on Monday, ignoring U.S. allegations that Taiwan had dumped memory chips in the United States, as investors hunted for bargains after Saturday's fall, brokers said.
The benchmark stock index, boosted by strong plastic and textile shares, finished 151.48 points or 1.78 percent higher to 8,639.37.
Turnover was a heavy T$166.68 billion.
Brokers said investors concentrated on trading industrial issues, including textile, plastics and paper shares. Financial shares also rebounded from a recent slide.

"Monday's market was largely a technical rebound from Saturday's fall," said vice president Wang Tung-liang of Jih Sun Securities. "Industrial shares, like textile, plastics, and paper, all had good performance after losing for a while."
Plastics shares rose 4.59 percent, textiles 3.95 percent and papers 3.22 percent.
Nan Ya Plastics rose T$4.5 to T$70. Chung Fu Textile rose T$1.7 to T$26.3 and Far Eastern Textile advanced T$3 to T$52. Chung Hwa Pulp gained T$1.9 to T$30.4.

Electronics gained slightly, still affected by allegations by U.S. International Trade Commission allegations that some Taiwan firms had dumped static random access memory chips -- sparking fears of a retaliatory anti-dumping tax.
Brokers said Saturday's 1.22 percent slide mainly reflected psychological jitters over Taiwan's crucial electronics sector.
Brokers expected share prices consolidate in the near term. A trading range of 8,520-8,620 was seen for Tuesday.
Brokers said the fledgling over-the-counter index was pulled higher by the main exchange's gains. It closed 1.06 points or 0.36 percent higher at 295.92. -- Lawrence Chung (5080815)
